text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Sale of state's 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF to be held through private placement with a book of terms and conditions.
-- Credit Lyonnais expects a 3.5-billion-franc profit for 1997 after an estimated 300-million-franc 1996 profit.
-- Arms manufacturer Giat Industries lost 1.3 billion francs in 1996, according to union sources.
-- Telecommunications minister Francois Fillon announces plans to introduce computers in schools on a large scale, confirms sale of France Telecom shares to begin in May.
-- Suez subsidiary Societe Generale de Belgique sells its 9 percent stake in hotels group Accor.
-- Amount of budget credit frozen in 1997 expected to be lower than previous years, estimated at between 9 and 14 billion francs, compared with 20 billion in 1996.
-- Paris court to look at bids for bank Pallas Stern today, which is currently under legal administration.
-- Survey shows small and medium-sized companies invest less in spite of rate cuts.
-- British investors skeptical about French pension funds if they are introduced without reform of the French banking system.
-- Customers turn away from life assurance, number of new contracts dropped 31 percent in 1996.
